summary: Learn project analysis, earned value, schedule forecasting, and Excel reporting. Explore the five-day course and build usable project deliverables.
lede: A project analyst course helps entry-level analysts, coordinators, and project support professionals turn project evidence into forecasts and decision records. Learners use baselines, earned value methods, and Excel to compare schedule and cost performance, track risks and dependencies, trace requirements and changes, and prepare concise decision reports. Portfolio analysis and advanced forecasting are covered at an introductory level.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people who prepare, check, or use project evidence in delivery decisions. It suits entry-level professionals who want a structured foundation in project data analysis, project controls, and reporting.
modules: Work Breakdown Structure and Scope Data
Critical Path Method and Schedule Analysis
RAID Log and Project Risk Analysis
Project Analyst Reporting and Decision Briefs
prerequisites: No prior project analyst role is required. Basic familiarity with workplace projects is helpful, but the course begins with foundational project analysis concepts. No coding or programming is required; exercises use project records and Excel.
